interactions.prompt:
You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]
  citation copied from the guidance spans below. Prefer a span of the current guidance, SR26-2;
  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

  "text": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing.   "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products\u2014including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models\u2014can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization\u2019s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation."

  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]",
  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper\u2019s judgment influences the model\u2019s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model\u2019s inherent risk. ## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a

5. **No sentence says a quantity is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a number is not
   available, not carried, not computed, not recomputed, absent, or missing is a failure — whether

   missing is not.

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

in your own words, what in the prose decided it. Three things it must not contain, because each of

The six-month mean payment ratio also agrees in sign, agreement 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], though refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], an improvement, so its contribution to ranking is not what its coefficient magnitude would suggest.
On balance the specification's discrimination is concentrated in delinquency status and utilisation, both signed as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms the model does not rely on.

Effective challenge was exercised with a histogram gradient boosting challenger on the same inputs.
The challenger reaches 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] in AUC against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], and it is also better calibrated in aggregate at a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The bound that decides whether such a gap matters is an AUC lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead is well past it.
This is finding E1, and because the challenger draws on the same features and differs only in admitting nonlinearity and interactions, the gap is evidence about the champion's functional form rather than about its inputs or its feature timing.
That finding is reported in the findings section, and the design assessment here should be read subject to it: the champion's construction is coherent and its economics read correctly, but a same-input nonlinear alternative extracts materially more discrimination from the same data."}

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a quantity is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a number is not
   available, not carried, not computed, not recomputed, absent, or missing is a failure — whether
   or not it is true of the list above. Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring it
   missing is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **one plain sentence** naming the criterion that decided the verdict and saying,
in your own words, what in the prose decided it. Three things it must not contain, because each of
them makes your reply unparseable and throws your verdict away:

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.
- **no line breaks.** One sentence, on one line.
- **no citations, backticks or code fences** copied out of the prose.

term" — never by quoting the line it sits on.

  "guidance": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing. While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments—such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models—may be more practical for other models. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. {"markdown": "Model design, key modeling choices, and the developmental evidence behind them are assessed here, together with a benchmark against an alternative approach [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].\n\nThe champion is a linear logit in its retained features, reported as a set of coefficients on an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows.\nThe subject's feature inventory carries 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in all.\nOf those, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.\nThe count first known during the performance period is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]] and the count first known only after the outcome is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on timing alone the design draws nothing that would be unavailable at scoring time.\n\nThe developer's own collinearity screen dropped `bill_last`, whose variance inflation factor was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and `utilisation_mean_6m`, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against a threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].\nBoth removals are the kind a validator would expect: each dropped feature is close to a linear combination of a retained billing or utilisation measure, and leaving them in would make individual coefficients unstable without adding information.\n\nThe largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on `delinq_last` at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by `bill_mean_6m` at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], `pay_ratio_mean_6m` at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], `utilisation` at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and `bill_trend_6m` at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].\nThe dominant term is the one credit subject matter would expect to dominate: the most recent delinquency status pushes the predicted probability of default up, and a heavier payment ratio averaged over the recent window pushes it down.\nA positive loading on utilisation is likewise what a credit analyst expects, since a borrower running closer to the limit is the riskier borrower.\nThe negative loading on average recent billing is less immediately intuitive but is consistent with the direction that measure takes on its own in the training data.\n\nThe fitted signs were compared against each feature's own univariate direction on train, and the two disagree for 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features.\nNo rule is applied to that comparison and none of what follows in this paragraph is a finding; the disagreements are read here as evidence about how much weight the champion's interpretation can bear, with each feature's ablation delta measured from a refit baseline test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]].\nThe coefficient on `limit_bal` is positive at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]] while its own relationship with the outcome on train runs the other way [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]], so the fitted model says a larger credit limit raises risk once the other features are held fixed, which is the opposite of the conventional underwriting reading.\nRefitting without that feature moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]] in the direction of a slightly better model, so the sign reversal sits on a feature the champion barely uses for discrimination.\nThe coefficient on `pay_ratio_last` is positive at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]] against a univariate direction that points down [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]], and refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement rather than a loss.\nThat pattern is the signature of a suppressor variable working against the six-month payment-ratio average it is correlated with, not of a feature carrying independent signal in the wrong direction.\nThe coefficient on `delinq_max_6m` is negative at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]] while the feature on its own points to higher risk [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]], which no credit reading supports; removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so the worst-delinquency measure is contributing almost nothing beyond the most recent delinquency status it duplicates.\nTaken together, all three reversals fall on features whose removal does not cost the model discrimination, so they are an interpretability caveat on the coefficient story rather than evidence that the model is leaning on a relationship backwards.\n\nThe features the champion actually depends on are the ones whose signs agree with their univariate directions.\nRemoving `delinq_last` costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC and removing `utilisation` costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], with `bill_mean_6m` costing -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].\nEvery other retained feature can be dropped without a loss, including `pay_ratio_mean_6m` at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], `bill_trend_6m` at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], `delinq_count_6m` at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] and `age` at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].\nThe design is therefore concentrated in a small number of delinquency and utilisation terms, with the remaining features contributing interpretive colour rather than discrimination.\n\nOn effective challenge, a histogram gradient boosting challenger reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]].\nThat is a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the difference therefore matters by the standard the run set for itself.\nThe challenger is also better calibrated on the same test data, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].\nBecause the challenger uses the same retained features and differs only in how it combines them, this margin is a statement about the champion's functional form rather than about its inputs or its screen: the linear logit is leaving nonlinearity and interaction on the table.\nThis is raised as finding E1, and the findings section carries it.\n\nSubject to that open question about functional form, the design is conceptually defensible: the timing of the inputs is sound, the collinearity screen is justified on its own terms, and the coefficients the model relies on carry the signs credit subject matter expects.\nThe three sign reversals and the concentration of discrimination in a handful of features are limitations on how far the fitted coefficients can be read as economic statements, and they should be documented as such wherever the model's output is explained to users."}

1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]
  citation copied from the guidance spans below. Prefer a span of the current guidance, SR26-2;
  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. ## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a quantity is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a number is not
   available, not carried, not computed, not recomputed, absent, or missing is a failure — whether
   or not it is true of the list above. Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring it
   missing is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **one plain sentence** naming the criterion that decided the verdict and saying,
in your own words, what in the prose decided it. Three things it must not contain, because each of
them makes your reply unparseable and throws your verdict away:

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.
- **no line breaks.** One sentence, on one line.
- **no citations, backticks or code fences** copied out of the prose.

{"markdown": "Design is assessed here as validation of conceptual soundness: the modelling choices, the construction, and the developmental evidence behind them, with interpretability measures and benchmarking against alternative models used where an appeal to theoretical construction alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### The champion and its inputs

The champion is a logistic regression for credit default, fitted with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and carrying a linear coefficient for each retained feature.
The feature inventory offered to the model holds 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features.
Of these, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none from after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing labels alone every input is available at the moment the score would be used.
The model's own collinearity screen then dropped two of the inventory before fitting.
The balance feature bill_last was dropped with a variance inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the averaged utilisation feature utilisation_mean_6m with 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Both removals are consistent with the reason such a screen exists: each dropped feature restates information already carried by a retained one, the last bill by the mean bill and the averaged utilisation by the point-in-time utilisation, and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable rather than more informative.
The screen's stated purpose is served, but it should be read as a variance-reduction device and not as evidence that the retained coefficients are individually interpretable.

### Coefficients and expected signs

The model leans hardest on recent delinquency, whose coefficient of 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]] is the largest in the fit and positive, which is the direction credit subject matter expects: a borrower delinquent in the most recent month is more likely to default.
The next largest are the mean bill over six months at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the mean payment ratio over six months at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]].
The negative sign on the payment ratio is what the subject matter expects, since a borrower who repays a larger share of the balance is the safer borrower.
The negative sign on the mean bill is less intuitive at face value, because a larger outstanding balance is usually read as more exposure and more risk; here it is more naturally read as conditional on utilisation and the delinquency terms, where a high absolute bill on a high limit is not the same signal as a high bill on a small limit.
Utilisation enters positively at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend negatively at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]], and the positive utilisation sign matches the expectation that borrowers pressed against their limit default more often.
The smaller terms are the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month delinquency maximum at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
Of these, the positive delinquency count and the negative age term read as expected, while a positive coefficient on the credit limit and a negative one on the worst delinquency in six months both run against what the subject matter would predict, since larger limits are typically extended to stronger borrowers and a worse delinquency peak is worse news.

### Sign checks and ablation as supporting evidence

The sign checks and the ablation deltas below are evidence bearing on the judgement in this section rather than the subject of any rule, and nothing in this subsection is a finding.
The fitted signs contradict the features' own univariate directions on train for 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features, and the magnitude of each disagreement is best read against how much discrimination that feature was carrying.
On the credit limit, the fitted coefficient is positive at 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own single-feature relationship with default points the other way at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], recorded as a disagreement at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting the champion's form without it changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the model was carrying no discrimination through this term and the flipped sign is a statement about a term the model barely uses.
On the six-month delinquency maximum, the fitted coefficient is negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], again a disagreement at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; dropping it moves test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so this term too contributes nothing the other delinquency features do not already carry, and the sign flip is most plausibly the residual of overlap with the last-month and count delinquency terms.
On the last payment ratio, the fitted coefficient is positive at 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], a disagreement at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it moves test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], the largest of the three and still an improvement, which points to this term absorbing a sign reversal relative to the six-month payment-ratio mean it sits alongside rather than to the model relying on it.
All three disagreements therefore fall on terms the model does not depend on for discrimination, which is a materially weaker concern than a sign flip on a load-bearing feature would be, though it does mean the individual coefficients on these three should not be quoted as economic effects.
The remaining retained features agree with their univariate directions: recent delinquency at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]] with a fitted sign of 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of 1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]]; utilisation at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]] with a fitted sign of 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of 1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]]; the six-month delinquency count at 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]] with a fitted sign of 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]]; the six-month payment ratio at 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]] with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]]; the six-month mean bill at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]] with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]]; the six-month bill trend at 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]] with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]]; and age at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]] with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] and a univariate direction of -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]].

The ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], the same level as the champion's recomputed test AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]].

### Effective challenge

Benchmarking against an alternative approach is the sharper test of this design, and it does not favour the champion.
A histogram gradient-boosting challenger reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]] measured against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]].

Because the challenger differs from the champion chiefly in functional form, allowing non-linearity and interactions that a linear-additive logistic specification cannot express, this gap is evidence about the champion's functional form rather than about its inputs, which both models draw from the same retained set.
This is finding E1, raised at low severity, and it is reported in the findings section; the assessment of conceptual soundness in this section is conditional on its disposition.
On the evidence here, the design is coherent and its load-bearing signs are defensible, but the functional form is not the best available representation of the relationship it is fitted to, and the concentration seen in the ablation deltas is consistent with a linear form leaving structure on the table.
"}

{"markdown": "Validating conceptual soundness here means assessing the champion's design, construction, and developmental evidence, and subjecting its modelling choices to critical analysis rather than accepting them as documented [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### Design and feature timing

The champion is a logistic regression: ten fitted coefficients on retained features over an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], estimated on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows.
Its declared feature inventory contains 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are dated after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing declared for these inputs the design does not use information that postdates the quantity it predicts.

The developer's own collinearity screen removed two features before fitting, judged against a variance-inflation ceiling of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold}].
The last billed amount was dropped at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation was dropped at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both removals are consistent with the screen as stated: each was a near-duplicate of a retained billing or utilisation measure, and dropping them protects the interpretability of the surviving coefficients rather than the model's discrimination.

### Coefficients and expected direction

The model's weight is concentrated in the delinquency and repayment block.
The largest coefficient is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive sign is what a credit analyst expects, since recent delinquency is the strongest ordinary marker of impending default.
The next largest are the six-month mean billed amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]].
The negative sign on the mean payment ratio is as expected, because a borrower who repays a larger share of the balance is the better risk.
Utilisation enters positively at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], which matches the expectation that a borrower closer to the limit is more likely to default, and the six-month billing trend enters at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The smaller weights are the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
The negative sign on the mean billed amount and on the maximum delinquency over six months both sit awkwardly with the subject-matter reading that larger balances and worse delinquency peaks raise risk, so each deserves the direction evidence set out below.

### Fitted signs against univariate direction

Across the retained features, three [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] fitted coefficients point in the opposite direction from the feature's own relationship with the outcome on train.
These direction comparisons are evidence for the design judgement rather than the subject of any rule, and the discrimination each disagreeing feature carries is read from a refit of the same functional form without it, measured from a baseline test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]].

The credit limit is fitted positive at 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own univariate direction is negative at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], recorded as a disagreement at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].
Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model is not leaning on the feature and the flipped sign most plausibly reflects the limit acting as a control on the other balance terms rather than as a risk driver in its own right.

The last payment ratio is fitted positive at 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a negative univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], again a disagreement at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
This is the most consequential of the three in interpretive terms, because the positive coefficient reads as "paying more raises default risk", yet removing the feature changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], which is to say the refit without it is no worse.
The six-month mean payment ratio, whose fitted sign agrees with its univariate direction at 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]] with both negative at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], appears to absorb the repayment signal and leave the single-month term with a residual, sign-flipped role.

The six-month maximum delinquency is fitted negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a positive univariate direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], a disagreement at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].
Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest of the three, and the flip is readily explained by its overlap with the two delinquency terms the model does rely on.

The remaining seven retained features agree with their univariate directions: the most recent delinquency status at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]] with coefficient sign 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and univariate direction 1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]]; utilisation at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]] with coefficient sign 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and univariate direction 1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]]; the six-month delinquency count at 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]] with coefficient sign 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] and univariate direction 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]]; the six-month mean billed amount at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]] with coefficient sign -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and univariate direction -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]]; the six-month billing trend at 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]] with coefficient sign -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] and univariate direction -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]]; and age at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]] with coefficient sign -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] and univariate direction -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]].
The negative sign on the mean billed amount is therefore internally consistent with the data even though it runs against the naive expectation, and the validator's reading is that it is picking up transactors with large revolving throughput and low distress rather than a balance-size effect.

### What the model actually uses

The ablation refits also locate the model's discrimination, which bears on whether its construction is proportionate to its inputs.
Only three retained features are carrying discrimination in the sense that removing them lowers test AUC: the most recent delinquency status at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean billed amount at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
The others are neutral or better removed, including the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month billing trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]], and age at 0.00008675 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
A specification in which most of the retained inputs contribute nothing to out-of-sample ranking is a legitimate design criticism even where no rule is triggered, and it should be read alongside the effective-challenge result below rather than separately from it.

### Effective challenge

The champion scores a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The challenger, a histogram gradient-boosting model fitted on the same retained features, reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], so it is both better at ranking and better calibrated on the same test data.
The lead is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]] above which the difference is treated as material.
The lead exceeds that threshold by roughly a factor of two and a half, which is the decisive conceptual-soundness result in this section: a flexible alternative on identical inputs extracts substantially more signal than the champion's linear-in-logit specification, so the shortfall is attributable to functional form rather than to the feature set.
This is raised as finding E1, and it is a finding about the champion's functional form; its severity, disposition, and any required remediation are reported in the findings section, and this section does not restate them.

### Assessment

The design is defensible in its inputs: the timing of the declared features is consistent with a model that predicts a forward outcome, the collinearity screen is applied against a stated ceiling and its two removals are justified by the magnitudes recorded, and the largest coefficient carries the sign that the credit-risk literature and ordinary underwriting judgement expect.
The weaknesses are in specification rather than in data selection: three fitted signs contradict their univariate directions, though in each case on a feature the refits show the model barely uses, and most retained features add no out-of-sample discrimination at all.
Against the guidance's expectation that benchmarking to other models is an appropriate way to test conceptual soundness where theoretical construction alone is not decisive [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]], the challenger comparison is the strongest evidence available here, and it does not support the champion's functional form as the best available representation of this relationship."}

The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. {"markdown": "Validating conceptual soundness means assessing and documenting the model's design, its key modeling choices and assumptions, its construction, and the developmental evidence behind it, and subjecting those aspects to critical analysis rather than accepting them as documented [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### Design and input timing

The champion is a linear logistic scorecard: a single linear index with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and one coefficient per retained feature, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and scored as a default probability.
The declared feature set contains 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts and 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are fixed at origination.
None are declared as observed during the performance period, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none as observed after the outcome, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the timing declaration alone, then, every input is available at the moment the score would be used, which is what a forward-looking application scorecard requires; the declaration is the developer's own labelling, and this section takes it as design evidence rather than as an independent test of it.

### The developer's own screen

The model's collinearity screen was run at a variance-inflation threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]] and removed two of the declared features before fitting.
The last bill amount was removed at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], far above that threshold, which is what one expects of a level that is nearly reconstructible from the retained six-month bill mean and bill trend.
The six-month mean utilisation was removed at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], again above the threshold and again close to a retained feature, the point-in-time utilisation.
Both removals are the kind of judgment this design should make: the screen drops the redundant member of each pair and keeps a spanning set, and it is documented with the diagnostic that motivated it.

### Fitted coefficients and expected signs

The largest coefficient in the fitted index is on the most recent delinquency status, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive direction is what credit subject matter expects: a customer currently behind is more likely to default.
The next largest are the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], the latter in the expected direction, since a customer who has been paying down a larger share of each statement is the better risk.
Utilisation enters at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], positive as expected, and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The remaining coefficients are smaller: the delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the latest payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
The negative sign on the six-month bill mean is worth flagging in words: a scorecard user would not read a higher average statement balance as protective on its own, and the sign is defensible only as a conditional effect once utilisation and the bill trend are in the index.

### Sign agreement and how much each disagreement matters

The sign evidence compares each fitted coefficient's direction with the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features disagree.
These comparisons and the refit deltas below are developmental evidence for the judgement in this section, not tests against a bound, and nothing in them is reported here as a finding.
Each refit delta is measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], so a negative delta means the feature was carrying discrimination and a positive delta means the refit without it scored slightly higher.

The credit limit is the first disagreement: its fitted sign is +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], recorded as disagreeing at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].
On its own a larger limit goes with lower default risk, as the univariate direction says and as an underwriter would expect, so the positive fitted coefficient runs against subject matter; dropping the feature moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model leans on it barely at all and the flip carries little consequence for the score.

The latest payment ratio is the second: fitted sign +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], disagreeing at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
This is the more interesting of the small disagreements, because the six-month mean of the same quantity enters with the expected negative sign, so the positive coefficient on the point-in-time version reads as a within-pair partialling effect rather than as a claim that paying more this month raises risk.
Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again a feature the model does not depend on.

The six-month maximum delinquency is the third: fitted sign -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], disagreeing at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].
A negative coefficient on a worst-delinquency measure is counter-intuitive on its face, and here too the natural reading is collinearity with the current delinquency status and the delinquency count, both of which enter positively; the refit without it moves test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest reliance of the three.

The two features the model actually depends on both agree with their univariate directions, which is the more important fact for interpretability.
The current delinquency status agrees at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC, by far the largest reliance in the model.
Utilisation agrees at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]].
The six-month bill mean also agrees at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], with fitted sign -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] matching a univariate direction of -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and it carries a modest amount of discrimination, -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Age, the six-month mean payment ratio, the bill trend and the delinquency count all agree as well, at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]], 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]] and 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]] respectively, with the payment-ratio mean fitted negative at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], age negative at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], the bill trend negative at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]], and the delinquency count positive at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].
Several of the agreeing features nonetheless contribute nothing the rest of the index does not already carry, since refits without them score slightly higher: 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]] for the payment-ratio mean, 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]] for the bill trend, 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] for the delinquency count, and 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]] for age.
Taken together, the design is a thin model in practice: discrimination is concentrated in the delinquency status and utilisation, and the remaining eight coefficients are close to free parameters whose signs should not be read as behavioural statements.

### Effective challenge

The champion scores a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
A histogram gradient-boosting challenger, fitted as the alternative methodology for this comparison, reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], so it is both better ordered and better calibrated on the same test data.
The lead is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]] of AUC, read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]] that decides whether such a difference is material, and it exceeds that threshold by more than double.
This is raised as a finding on effective challenge, and because the challenger differs from the champion chiefly in functional form, the finding is in substance about the champion's functional form: a linear index in these features leaves a material amount of the available discrimination unused, most plausibly non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency and utilisation measures.
That finding, its severity and its disposition are reported in the findings section, which is where the reader should go for it.
The more general judgement of this section is that the design is defensible in its inputs, its timing and its collinearity screen, that its coefficient signs are interpretable except for three small-reliance disagreements described above, and that its choice of functional form is where the effective-challenge evidence pushes back hardest."}

A negative coefficient on a worst-delinquency measure is counter-intuitive on its face, and here too the natural reading is collinearity with the current delinquency status and the delinquency count, both of which enter positively; the refit without it moves test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest reliance of the three.

The two features the model actually depends on both agree with their univariate directions, which is the more important fact for interpretability.
The current delinquency status agrees at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC, by far the largest reliance in the model.
Utilisation agrees at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]].
The six-month bill mean also agrees at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], with fitted sign -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] matching a univariate direction of -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and it carries a modest amount of discrimination, -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Age, the six-month mean payment ratio, the bill trend and the delinquency count all agree as well, at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]], 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]] and 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]] respectively, with the payment-ratio mean fitted negative at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], age negative at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], the bill trend negative at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]], and the delinquency count positive at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].
Several of the agreeing features nonetheless contribute nothing the rest of the index does not already carry, since refits without them score slightly higher: 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]] for the payment-ratio mean, 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]] for the bill trend, 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] for the delinquency count, and 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]] for age.
Taken together, the design is a thin model in practice: discrimination is concentrated in the delinquency status and utilisation, and the remaining eight coefficients are close to free parameters whose signs should not be read as behavioural statements.

### Effective challenge

The champion scores a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
A histogram gradient-boosting challenger, fitted as the alternative methodology for this comparison, reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], so it is both better ordered and better calibrated on the same test data.
The lead is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]] of AUC, read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]] that decides whether such a difference is material, and it exceeds that threshold by more than double.
This is raised as a finding on effective challenge, and because the challenger differs from the champion chiefly in functional form, the finding is in substance about the champion's functional form: a linear index in these features leaves a material amount of the available discrimination unused, most plausibly non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency and utilisation measures.
That finding, its severity and its disposition are reported in the findings section, which is where the reader should go for it.
The more general judgement of this section is that the design is defensible in its inputs, its timing and its collinearity screen, that its coefficient signs are interpretable except for three small-reliance disagreements described above, and that its choice of functional form is where the effective-challenge evidence pushes back hardest."}

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
