  "guidance": "Validating  conceptual  soundness  involves  assessing  and  documenting  model  design\n(including  key  modeling  choices,  assumptions,  qualitative  judgments,  and  data  selection),\nconstruction,  and  developmental  testing.  While  evaluating  theoretical  construction  may  be\nimportant  for  some  models,  other  assessments—such  as  interpretability  measures  or\nbenchmarking  to  other  models—may  be  more  practical  for  other  models.  Sound  practice  subjects\nmodeling  aspects  to  critical  analysis  by  evaluating  both  the  quality  and  extent  of  developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe  widespread  use  of  customized  vendor  and  other  third-party  products—including\ndata,  parameter  values,  or  complete  models—can  present  unique  challenges  for  validation  and\nother  model  risk  management  activities.  Additionally,  because  certain  components  may  be\nproprietary,  banking  organizations  may  not  receive  from  the  vendor  the  underlying  code,  data,  or\nmethodology  that  they  would  have  if  a  model  were  developed  internally.  Nevertheless,  the\nprinciples  of  model  risk  management  remain  applicable.\nAn  important  element  of  model  risk  management  is  the  validation  of  vendor  products,\neither  by  internal  or  outside  parties.  Sound  practice  includes  developing  an  understanding  of  the\nvendor  model,  including  its  conceptual  soundness,  design,  development  data,  and  performance.\nSimilarly,  sound  practice  involves  conducting  ongoing  monitoring  and  outcome  analysis  to\nassess  whether  vendor  models  are  accurate,  remain  fit  for  purpose,  and  continue  to  be  reliable.\nSuch  analysis  can  also  be  used  to  support  any  overlay  or  adjustment  to  model  output.  In  cases\nwhere  vendor  models  are  customized  to  fit  a  banking  organization’s  specific  business  needs,\nsound  practice  also  involves  appropriately  documenting,  justifying,  and  evaluating  adjustments\nmade  to  customize  the  model  as  part  of  model  validation.\n\n---\n\nSound  model  development  activities  are  aligned  with  model  purpose,  business  use,  and\nbanking  organization  policy.  Model  development  is  not  purely  a  technical  exercise.  The\ndeveloper’s  judgment  influences  the  model’s  conceptual  design  and  soundness,  inputs,\nassumptions,  and  methodology,  all  of  which  affect  a  model’s  inherent  risk.  Because  model\ndevelopment  is  often  multidisciplinary,  tailored  to  actual  use,  and  involves  significant\nsubjectivity  throughout  its  lifecycle,  sound  development  practices  are  important  for  effective\nmodel  risk  management.\nAn  effective  development  process  generally  begins  with  a  clear  statement  of  purpose  to\nmaximize  the  likelihood  that  model  development  is  aligned  with  the  intended  use.  This\nfundamental  step  supports  decision-making  throughout  the  development  lifecycle,  including  the\nselection  of  data,  methodologies,  and  testing  approaches.\nInput  from  model  users  can  enhance  model  development  by  providing  business  context\nand  practical  insights.  Business  managers  affected  by  model  outcomes  may  raise  questions  about\nthe  methods  or  assumptions,  particularly  when  the  outcomes  are  unexpected.  Constructive\nengagement  around  model  design  and  assumptions  strengthens  both  model  understanding  and\nmodel  quality.\nModel  testing  is  a  core  component  of  model  development  that  evaluates  whether  a  model\nperforms  as  intended.  Testing  may  include  a  range  of  activities,  from  out-of-sample  and  out-of-\ntime  testing,  to  a  comparison  of  alternative  assumptions  and  methodologies,  to  a  critical\nassessment  of  data  quality,  relevance,  and  inputs.  Testing  may  be  performed  by  model\ndevelopers  in  collaboration  with  model  users.  The  specific  approach  depends  on  the  model’s\ncharacteristics.  The  rigor  of  effective  testing  is  commensurate  with  model  complexity  and\nmateriality.  For  models  that  have  relatively  less  material  impact  or  for  banking  organizations\nwith  relatively  less  complex  operations,  model  testing  may  be  more  limited  in  scope.\n\n---\n\nThis  element  involves  assessing  the  quality  of  the  model  design  and  construction.  It\nentails  review  of  documentation  and  empirical  evidence  supporting  the  methods  used  and\nvariables  selected  for  the  model.  Documentation  and  testing  should  convey  an\nunderstanding  of  model  limitations  and  assumptions.  Validation  should  ensure  that\njudgment  exercised  in  model  design  and  construction  is  well  informed,  carefully\nconsidered,  and  consistent  with  published  research  and  with  sound  industry  practice.\nDevelopmental  evidence  should  be  reviewed  before  a  model  goes  into  use  and  also  as\npart  of  the  ongoing  validation  process,  in  particular  whenever  there  is  a  material  change\nin  the  model.\nA  sound  development  process  will  produce  documented  evidence  in  support  of  all  model\nchoices,  including  the  overall  theoretical  construction,  key  assumptions,  data,  and\nspecific  mathematical  calculations,  as  mentioned  in  Section  IV.  As  part  of  model\nvalidation,  those  model  aspects  should  be  subjected  to  critical  analysis  by  both  evaluating\nthe  quality  and  extent  of  developmental  evidence  and  conducting  additional  analysis  and\ntesting  as  necessary.  Comparison  to  alternative  theories  and  approaches  should  be\nincluded.  Key  assumptions  and  the  choice  of  variables  should  be  assessed,  with  analysis\nof  their  impact  on  model  outputs  and  particular  focus  on  any  potential  limitations.  The\nrelevance  of  the  data  used  to  build  the  model  should  be  evaluated  to  ensure  that  it  is\nreasonably  representative  of  the  bank's  portfolio  or  market  conditions,  depending  on  the\ntype  of  model.  This  is  an  especially  important  exercise  when  a  bank  uses  external  data  or\nthe  model  is  used  for  new  products  or  activities.\nWhere  appropriate  to  the  particular  model,  banks  should  employ  sensitivity  analysis  in\nmodel  development  and  validation  to  check  the  impact  of  small  changes  in  inputs  and\nparameter  values  on  model  outputs  to  make  sure  they  fall  within  an  expected  range.\nUnexpectedly  large  changes  in  outputs  in  response  to  small  changes  in  inputs  can  indicate\nan  unstable  model.  Varying  several  inputs  simultaneously  as  part  of  sensitivity  analysis\ncan  provide  evidence  of  unexpected  interactions,  particularly  if  the  interactions  are\ncomplex  and  not  intuitively  clear.  Banks  benefit  from  conducting  model  stress  testing  to\ncheck  performance  over  a  wide  range  of  inputs  and  parameter  values,  including  extreme\nvalues,  to  verify  that  the  model  is  robust.  Such  testing  helps  establish  the  boundaries  of\nmodel  performance  by  identifying  the  acceptable  range  of  inputs  as  well  as  conditions\nunder  which  the  model  may  become  unstable  or  inaccurate.\nManagement  should  have  a  clear  plan  for  using  the  results  of  sensitivity  analysis  and\nother  quantitative  testing.  If  testing  indicates  that  the  model  may  be  inaccurate  or  unstable\nin  some  circumstances,  management  should  consider  modifying  certain  model  properties,  [Page  Break]\nputting  less  reliance  on  its  outputs,  placing  limits  on  model  use,  or  developing  a  new\napproach.\nQualitative  information  and  judgment  used  in  model  development  should  be  evaluated,\nincluding  the  logic,  judgment,  and  types  of  information  used,  to  establish  the  conceptual\nsoundness  of  the  model  and  set  appropriate  conditions  for  its  use.  The  validation  process\nshould  ensure  that  qualitative,  judgmental  assessments  are  conducted  in  an  appropriate\nand  systematic  manner,  are  well  supported,  and  are  documented.\n\n---\n\nAn  effective  validation  framework  should  include  three  core  elements:\n•  Evaluation  of  conceptual  soundness,  including  developmental  evidence\n•  Ongoing  monitoring,  including  process  verification  and  benchmarking\n•  Outcomes  analysis,  including  back-testing\n\n---\n\nModel  risk  management  should  include  disciplined  and  knowledgeable  development  and\nimplementation  processes  that  are  consistent  with  the  situation  and  goals  of  the  model\nuser  and  with  bank  policy.  Model  development  is  not  a  straightforward  or  routine\ntechnical  process.  The  experience  and  judgment  of  developers,  as  much  as  their  technical\nknowledge,  greatly  influence  the  appropriate  selection  of  inputs  and  processing\ncomponents.  The  training  and  experience  of  developers  exercising  such  judgment  affects\nthe  extent  of  model  risk.  Moreover,  the  modeling  exercise  is  often  a  multidisciplinary\nactivity  drawing  on  economics,  finance,  statistics,  mathematics,  and  other  fields.  Models\nare  employed  in  real-world  markets  and  events  and  therefore  should  be  tailored  for\nspecific  applications  and  informed  by  business  uses.  In  addition,  a  considerable  amount\nof  subjective  judgment  is  exercised  at  various  stages  of  model  development,\nimplementation,  use,  and  validation.  It  is  important  for  decision  makers  to  recognize  that\nthis  subjectivity  elevates  the  importance  of  sound  and  comprehensive  model  risk\nmanagement  processes.  [Footnote  4\n-  Smaller  banks  that  rely  on  vendor  models  may  be  able  to  satisfy  the  standards  in  this  guidance  without  an\nin-house  staff  of  technical,  quantitative  model  developers.  However,  even  if  a  bank  relies  on  vendors  for\nbasic  model  development,  the  bank  should  still  choose  the  particular  models  and  variables  that  are\nappropriate  to  its  size,  scale,  and  lines  of  business  and  ensure  the  models  are  appropriate  for  the  intended\nuse.  End  of  Footnote  4.]\n\n",

{"markdown": "Sound validation of conceptual soundness assesses and documents model design, key modeling choices, assumptions and developmental evidence, and where theoretical construction is less informative it leans on interpretability measures and benchmarking to other models [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].\n\n### Design and inputs\n\nThe champion is a coefficient-based, linear-in-parameters scorer with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and a coefficient on each retained feature, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, and it produces a calibrated probability whose recomputed test discrimination is 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].\nIts input specification names 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.\nNo input is drawn from inside the performance window, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none is drawn from after the outcome is known, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so the timing of the inputs is consistent with a score that could be formed at decision time.\n\n### The collinearity screen\n\nThe developer's own screen dropped the most recent bill amount, whose variance-inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]] sat far above the screen's bound of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]], and the six-month mean of utilisation, whose variance-inflation factor of 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]] also exceeded that bound.\nBoth removals are defensible on their face: each dropped term is close to a linear combination of terms that were kept, and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable and their signs uninterpretable.\nThe consequence for this section is that the retained coefficients must be read as partial effects conditional on near-duplicate information having been removed, not as standalone risk relationships.\n\n### The largest coefficients and their signs\n\nThe largest coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], which is positive as credit judgement expects, since a borrower currently behind is more likely to default.\nThe next largest are the six-month mean bill amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], and the negative sign on a sustained payment ratio is what the subject matter expects, since a The declared feature set has 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] members, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period opens.

That is the right shape for a forward-looking default score, and it is the single most important design property to have established before any of the performance numbers are read.

The developer's own collinearity screen dropped two inputs before fitting.
It removed bill_last, whose variance inflation was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and utilisation_mean_6m, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against the screen's own cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].

The largest coefficient by magnitude sits on delinq_last at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], well clear of the rest of the vector.

The comparison between each fitted sign and the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and the change in test AUC when the champion's form is refitted without a feature, are evidence supporting the judgement in this section rather than the subject of any rule, and nothing described in this subsection is a finding.
The ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test.

The fitted sign on pay_ratio_last is positive, 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]], against a negative univariate direction, -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
This is the sharper of the three to explain, because the averaged payment ratio in the same model keeps the expected negative sign, so the point-in-time term is reading as a residual against that average rather than as a level effect.

The fitted sign on delinq_max_6m is negative, -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]], against a positive univariate direction, 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].

### Effective challenge

The champion reaches an AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] on test with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
A histogram gradient boosting challenger, fitted for comparison on the same retained inputs, reaches an AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], better on both discrimination and calibration-sensitive accuracy.

That gap is finding E1.

E1 is a finding about the champion's functional form, and this section flags it as such.
The challenger sees the same inputs at the same timing and differs from the champion principally in that it can represent non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency, utilisation and billing blocks, which a single linear index cannot; the size of the gap is therefore evidence that the linear specification, not the feature set, is what limits the champion.
The over-specified periphery documented above points the same way, since a form that must express every effect as a constant log-odds slope will spend weight on terms that do not generalise.
The findings section reports E1, its severity and its disposition, and this section does not restate them.

### Judgement

On design, the champion is transparent, its inputs are all knowable before the performance window opens, and its collinearity screen is justified on the evidence presented.
On direction, the terms that carry the model's discrimination behave as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms whose removal does not cost the model anything measurable on test.
The substantive reservation from this section is the functional form, which the effective-challenge comparison addresses and which is carried into the findings section as E1; the sign disagreements and the negative-contribution terms are recorded here as design observations for the developer to address at the next refit."}

1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]
  citation copied from the guidance spans below. Prefer a span of the current guidance, SR26-2;
  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a quantity is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a number is not
   available, not carried, not computed, not recomputed, absent, or missing is a failure — whether

   missing is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **one plain sentence** naming the criterion that decided the verdict and saying,
in your own words, what in the prose decided it. Three things it must not contain, because each of

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.
- **no line breaks.** One sentence, on one line.
- **no citations, backticks or code fences** copied out of the prose.

### Design and inputs

The champion is a linear-in-the-parameters scorer with an estimated intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training records and scoring 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] AUC and 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] Brier on test as recomputed here.

No feature is drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none is drawn from after the outcome is determined, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the declared timing alone the input set is available at the point the score would be used.
The developer's own collinearity screen removed two features against a variance-inflation cut-off of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]]: the last bill amount, whose inflation factor was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both removals are defensible on their face, since each removed feature is close to a linear combination of retained ones — the last bill against the six-month bill mean and trend, and mean utilisation against point-in-time utilisation — and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable rather than more informative.
The screen is nonetheless a design choice with a consequence for interpretation: the retained utilisation and bill terms now absorb the explanatory content of their removed near-duplicates, so individual coefficients should be read as loadings on a correlated block rather than as isolated effects.

The largest fitted weight by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency state, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].

The six-month maximum delinquency enters with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against an own direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]], and removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]].

None of the sign or ablation evidence in this subsection is a finding; it is the developmental evidence against which the design judgement is made.

### Effective challenge

A hist_gradient_boosting challenger reaches 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] AUC on test against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]].

This exceedance is raised as a finding and is reported in the findings section, which is where its severity and disposition are recorded.
The threshold above is the bound that decides whether the difference matters, and on the evidence here the difference is material to the choice of functional form rather than a marginal preference between two adequate designs.

### Assessment

The input timing, the documented collinearity screen, and the direction of the model's heaviest weights support the design as a defensible, interpretable specification for this purpose.
Against that, three sign contradictions, a specification in which most terms contribute little or negatively to discrimination, and a materially stronger non-linear benchmark together indicate that the champion's functional form is the weakest part of its conceptual case, and the developmental evidence would be strengthened by a documented comparison of alternative forms rather than by further tuning of this one."}

### Design and inputs

The champion is a linear-in-the-parameters scorer with an estimated intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training records and scoring 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] AUC and 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] Brier on test as recomputed here.

No feature is drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none is drawn from after the outcome is determined, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the declared timing alone the input set is available at the point the score would be used.
The developer's own collinearity screen removed two features against a variance-inflation cut-off of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]]: the last bill amount, whose inflation factor was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both removals are defensible on their face, since each removed feature is close to a linear combination of retained ones — the last bill against the six-month bill mean and trend, and mean utilisation against point-in-time utilisation — and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable rather than more informative.
The screen is nonetheless a design choice with a consequence for interpretation: the retained utilisation and bill terms now absorb the explanatory content of their removed near-duplicates, so individual coefficients should be read as loadings on a correlated block rather than as isolated effects.

### Coefficients and expected direction

The largest fitted weight by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency state, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The remaining weights are smaller: the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a quantity is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a number is not
   available, not carried, not computed, not recomputed, absent, or missing is a failure — whether
   or not it is true of the list above. Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring it
   missing is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **one plain sentence** naming the criterion that decided the verdict and saying,
in your own words, what in the prose decided it. Three things it must not contain, because each of

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.

While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments—such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models—may be more practical for other models. Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model. Varying several inputs simultaneously as part of sensitivity analysis\ncan provide evidence of unexpected interactions, particularly if the interactions are\ncomplex and not intuitively clear. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust. Such testing helps establish the boundaries of\nmodel performance by identifying the acceptable range of inputs as well as conditions\nunder which the model may become unstable or inaccurate.\nManagement should have a clear plan for using the results of sensitivity analysis and\nother quantitative testing. In addition, a considerable amount\nof subjective judgment is exercised at various stages of model development,\nimplementation, use, and validation. removed two of the candidates before fitting: the most recent bill amount, whose variance inflation factor was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's ceiling of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].\nBoth removals are defensible on their face, since each dropped feature is close to an algebraic restatement of a feature that was retained, and removing them leaves the retained set interpretable coefficient by coefficient.\nThe champion is a linear-in-log-odds scorecard over the retained features, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month mean bill at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].\nThe remaining weights are an order smaller: the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the most recent payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]] and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 Both removals are intelligible given what was retained, since the last bill amount is close to the six-month bill mean and mean utilisation is close to the point-in-time utilisation that was kept, so the screen removed redundancy rather than distinct risk content.

The negative direction on the six-month mean payment ratio is also what the subject matter expects, since repaying a larger share of the bill should lower default risk.
The negative directions on the six-month bill mean and bill trend are less obviously signed on subject matter grounds, since a larger or rising balance can reflect either spending capacity or strain, and both agree with their own univariate direction on train, -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]].

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

A gradient-boosting challenger fitted on the same retained features reaches an AUC on test of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]].
The challenger is also better calibrated in the aggregate, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The threshold that decides whether an effective-challenge gap matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead exceeds it by more than a factor of two.
This is finding E1, and it is a statement about the champion's functional form: a model of identical inputs with a form that admits non-linearity and interaction recovers substantially more discrimination, which points at the linear-additive specification rather than at the data or the feature set.
The ablation pattern above is consistent with that reading, since the linear form extracts almost nothing from seven of its ten inputs.
The finding is carried in the findings section, where its severity and disposition are recorded; this section reports only the evidence for it."}

A higher six-month mean payment ratio lowers risk, at a fitted sign of -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and older borrowers default less, at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]]; the six-month bill mean and bill trend also agree, at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]] respectively, as does the six-month delinquency count at +1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against +1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].

Of the ten retained coefficients, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] carry a fitted sign that contradicts the feature's own direction on train.
The credit limit is fitted positive at +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own relationship with default on train runs the other way at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the agreement indicator is 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting the champion's form without it moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the model is not leaning on this feature and the reversal reads as the limit acting as a conditioning variable once utilisation is in the equation rather than as a risk driver in its own right.
The last payment ratio is fitted positive at +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement, and the sign is plausibly absorbed by the six-month mean payment ratio, which carries the same construct with the larger weight and the expected sign.
The six-month maximum delinquency is fitted negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], with an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so this is the smallest weight in the model attached to the least-used feature, and the negative sign next to a positive and much larger weight on the most recent delinquency status is the arithmetic of two overlapping delinquency measures rather than a claim that worse past delinquency lowers risk.
All three reversals sit on features the model barely uses, which is materially different from a reversal on a feature carrying discrimination; none of the three has a negative ablation delta.

### What the model actually leans on

Measured from a refit baseline of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test, only three features lose the model discrimination when removed: the most recent delinquency status at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]] and the six-month bill mean at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Every other retained feature leaves test AUC unchanged or slightly better when dropped, including the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month bill trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] and age at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
The model's discrimination therefore rests on a narrow base of recent delinquency and current utilisation, with the remaining seven inputs contributing little or nothing on test, and the three sign reversals all fall in that second group.

### Effective challenge

A gradient-boosting challenger fitted on the same retained features reaches an AUC on test of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]].
The challenger is also better calibrated in the aggregate, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The threshold that decides whether an effective-challenge gap matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead exceeds it by more than a factor of two.
This is finding E1, and it is a statement about the champion's functional form: a model of identical inputs with a form that admits non-linearity and interaction recovers substantially more discrimination, which points at the linear-additive specification rather than at the data or the feature set.
The ablation pattern above is consistent with that reading, since the linear form extracts almost nothing from seven of its ten inputs.
The finding is carried in the findings section, where its severity and disposition are recorded; this section reports only the evidence for it."}

written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that an **analysis does not apply to this model type** — a cross-regime stability comparison
     where no regime column is declared, rate-shock scenarios where the subject is not a hazard
     model. The section is asked for exactly this and the report's Appendix D records it.
   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

{"markdown": "Assessment of design here follows the guidance's expectation that validation assess and document model design, construction, and developmental testing, and subject modeling choices to critical analysis of both the quality and extent of developmental evidence [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### Design and feature timing

The champion is a logistic regression fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and ten retained coefficients.
The subject's feature inventory carries 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in total.
Of these, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are dated after the outcome, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the timing evidence given, every feature the model uses is knowable at scoring time, which is the design property that matters for a forward-looking default score.

### The developer's own screen

The developer screened for collinearity against a variance-inflation cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Two features were removed on that screen: the last bill amount, at 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both sit well above the cutoff, and both are near-duplicates of retained features, so removing them is a defensible choice that leaves the retained block interpretable rather than one that discards independent signal.

### Coefficients and expected signs

The largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency indicator, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], positive as credit subject matter expects: recent delinquency raises default risk.
The next largest are the six-month mean bill amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
A negative loading on the mean payment ratio and a positive loading on utilisation are both what a credit reviewer would expect, since paying down more of the balance lowers risk and running closer to the limit raises it.
The remaining coefficients are smaller: the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].

Against each feature's own univariate direction on train, three [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the ten retained coefficients carry a sign that contradicts that direction.
These are evidence for the design judgement rather than the subject of any rule, and none of them is reported here as a finding.

The credit limit's fitted sign is positive at 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is negative at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the two do not agree, at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].
Refitting the champion's form without the credit limit changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model is not leaning on the feature and the reversal costs little discrimination either way.

The last payment ratio's fitted sign is positive at 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is negative at -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], again a disagreement, at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
Dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], an improvement rather than a loss, so the fitted positive loading is best read as a conditional adjustment alongside the six-month mean payment ratio rather than as a claim that paying more raises risk.

The six-month maximum delinquency's fitted sign is negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is positive at 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], the third disagreement, at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].
This is the sign reversal a reviewer would question hardest, since a worse peak delinquency lowering the fitted score is contrary to credit expectation, but removing the feature changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so the model barely uses it and the reversal is a presentational and explainability concern rather than a driver of the score.
All three reversals sit on features the delinquency and payment blocks already cover, which is the ordinary consequence of correlated inputs surviving a collinearity screen at a cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].

The seven remaining coefficients agree with their univariate directions.
Recent delinquency is positive on both, at 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]].
Utilisation is positive on both, at 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]].
The six-month delinquency count is positive on both, at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]].
Age is negative on both, at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]].
The six-month mean payment ratio is negative on both, at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]].
The six-month mean bill amount is negative on both, at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]].
The six-month bill trend is negative on both, at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]].

### What the model actually depends on

Refitting the champion's functional form on every retained feature gives a test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], the level each ablation delta is measured from, and matching the champion's recomputed test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]].
Only three features carry discrimination in the sense that removing them lowers that level: recent delinquency at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean bill amount at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Removing recent delinquency costs almost as much AUC as the champion holds over the challenger's lead, which tells the reader that the design is in substance a recent-delinquency model with utilisation as a secondary driver.
The other retained features do not lower test AUC when dropped: the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month bill trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the last payment ratio at 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]], the credit limit at 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], the six-month maximum delinquency at 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], and age at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
A specification in which most retained terms are not carrying test discrimination is a parsimony question for the developer, and it is the same set of terms on which the sign reversals sit.

### Effective challenge

The guidance treats benchmarking to other models as a practical form of critical analysis where evaluating theoretical construction alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].
A gradient-boosting challenger reaches a test AUC of 0.8240 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]].
The threshold that decides whether such a difference matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead is roughly two and a half times that bound.
The same ordering holds on calibration, where the challenger's Brier score is 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]], lower being better, so the gap is not an artefact of the ranking metric alone.

This gap is a finding on the champion's functional form, raised as E1 at suggested severity low, and it is reported in full in the findings section.
In conceptual terms it says that the additive linear form the developer chose leaves structure in the data — interactions and non-linearities in the delinquency and utilisation blocks — that a flexible learner recovers, and the sign reversals discussed above are consistent with a linear form absorbing correlated inputs it cannot represent separately.
The design remains explainable and its timing discipline is sound, but the developmental evidence does not show that the chosen form is the best available one for this portfolio, and the section's judgement is that conceptual soundness is acceptable only with the functional-form question left open for the findings section to carry."}
