The remaining coefficients are smaller: the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].

Against each feature's own univariate direction on train, three [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the ten retained coefficients carry a sign that contradicts that direction.
These are evidence for the design judgement rather than the subject of any rule, and none of them is reported here as a finding.

The credit limit's fitted sign is positive at 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is negative at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the two do not agree, at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].
Refitting the champion's form without the credit limit changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model is not leaning on the feature and the reversal costs little discrimination either way.

The last payment ratio's fitted sign is positive at 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is negative at -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], again a disagreement, at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
Dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], an improvement rather than a loss, so the fitted positive loading is best read as a conditional adjustment alongside the six-month mean payment ratio rather than as a claim that paying more raises risk.

The six-month maximum delinquency's fitted sign is negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] while its univariate direction is positive at 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], the third disagreement, at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].
This is the sign reversal a reviewer would question hardest, since a worse peak delinquency lowering the fitted score is contrary to credit expectation, but removing the feature changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so the model barely uses it and the reversal is a presentational and explainability concern rather than a driver of the score.
All three reversals sit on features the delinquency and payment blocks already cover, which is the ordinary consequence of correlated inputs surviving a collinearity screen at a cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].

The seven remaining coefficients agree with their univariate directions.
Recent delinquency is positive on both, at 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]].
Utilisation is positive on both, at 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]].
The six-month delinquency count is positive on both, at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] and 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]].
Age is negative on both, at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]].
The six-month mean payment ratio is negative on both, at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]].
The six-month mean bill amount is negative on both, at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]].
The six-month bill trend is negative on both, at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] and -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]], agreeing at 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]].

### What the model actually depends on

Refitting the champion's functional form on every retained feature gives a test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], the level each ablation delta is measured from, and matching the champion's recomputed test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]].
Only three features carry discrimination in the sense that removing them lowers that level: recent delinquency at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean bill amount at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Removing recent delinquency costs almost as much AUC as the champion holds over the challenger's lead, which tells the reader that the design is in substance a recent-delinquency model with utilisation as a secondary driver.
The other retained features do not lower test AUC when dropped: the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month bill trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the last payment ratio at 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]], the credit limit at 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], the six-month maximum delinquency at 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], and age at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
A specification in which most retained terms are not carrying test discrimination is a parsimony question for the developer, and it is the same set of terms on which the sign reversals sit.

### Effective challenge

The guidance treats benchmarking to other models as a practical form of critical analysis where evaluating theoretical construction alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].
A gradient-boosting challenger reaches a test AUC of 0.8240 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]].
The threshold that decides whether such a difference matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead is roughly two and a half times that bound.
The same ordering holds on calibration, where the challenger's Brier score is 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]], lower being better, so the gap is not an artefact of the ranking metric alone.

This gap is a finding on the champion's functional form, raised as E1 at suggested severity low, and it is reported in full in the findings section.
In conceptual terms it says that the additive linear form the developer chose leaves structure in the data — interactions and non-linearities in the delinquency and utilisation blocks — that a flexible learner recovers, and the sign reversals discussed above are consistent with a linear form absorbing correlated inputs it cannot represent separately.
The design remains explainable and its timing discipline is sound, but the developmental evidence does not show that the chosen form is the best available one for this portfolio, and the section's judgement is that conceptual soundness is acceptable only with the functional-form question left open for the findings section to carry."}

You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that an **analysis does not apply to this model type** — a cross-regime stability comparison
     where no regime column is declared, rate-shock scenarios where the subject is not a hazard
     model. The section is asked for exactly this and the report's Appendix D records it.
   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **at most fifteen words**: name the criterion that decided the verdict and, in a
few words of your own, what decided it. Nothing longer. A long rationale is the single commonest
way this reply comes back unparseable — measured at 80% and then 25% of replies on two recordings
of this suite — so brevity is the requirement, not a preference.

Four things it must not contain, because each of them throws your verdict away:

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.
- **no line breaks.** One short clause, on one line.
- **no citations, backticks, braces or code fences** copied out of the prose.
- **nothing at all after the closing brace.** Emit exactly one object. If you decide your first

closes with a brace. A missing closing quote discards a verdict you got right.

  "guidance": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing. While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments—such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models—may be more practical for other models. Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model. Varying several inputs simultaneously as part of sensitivity analysis\ncan provide evidence of unexpected interactions, particularly if the interactions are\ncomplex and not intuitively clear. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust. Such testing helps establish the boundaries of\nmodel performance by identifying the acceptable range of inputs as well as conditions\nunder which the model may become unstable or inaccurate.\nManagement should have a clear plan for using the results of sensitivity analysis and\nother quantitative testing. If testing indicates that the model may be inaccurate or unstable\nin some circumstances, management should consider modifying certain model properties, [Page Break]\nputting less reliance on its outputs, placing limits on model use, or developing a new\napproach.\nQualitative information and judgment used in model development should be evaluated,\nincluding the logic, judgment, and types of information used, to establish the conceptual\nsoundness of the model and set appropriate conditions for its use. The validation process\nshould ensure that qualitative, judgmental assessments are conducted in an appropriate\nand systematic manner, are well supported, and are documented.\n\n---\n\nAn effective validation framework should include three core elements:\n• Evaluation of conceptual soundness, including developmental evidence\n• Ongoing monitoring, including process verification and benchmarking\n• Outcomes analysis, including back-testing\n\n---\n\nModel risk management should include disciplined and knowledgeable development and\nimplementation processes that are consistent with the situation and goals of the model\nuser and with bank policy. Model development is not a straightforward or routine\ntechnical process. The experience and judgment of developers, as much as their technical\nknowledge, greatly influence the appropriate selection of inputs and processing\ncomponents. The training and experience of developers exercising such judgment affects\nthe extent of model risk. Moreover, the modeling exercise is often a multidisciplinary\nactivity drawing on economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, and other fields. Models\nare employed in real-world markets and events and therefore should be tailored for\nspecific applications and informed by business uses. In addition, a considerable amount\nof subjective judgment is exercised at various stages of model development,\nimplementation, use, and validation. It is important for decision makers to recognize that\nthis subjectivity elevates the importance of sound and comprehensive model risk\nmanagement processes. # Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this

   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold

   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this

section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model. {"markdown": "Validating conceptual soundness means assessing and documenting the model's design — its key modelling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments and data selection — together with its construction and developmental testing, and this section does that for the credit_default champion by examining its inputs, its fitted coefficients, and its performance against a challenger. [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]\n\n### Design and inputs\n\nThe champion is a single linear scoring model in the log-odds, carrying one fitted coefficient per retained feature plus an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], estimated on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows.\nThe declared feature set has 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] members, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period opens.\nThe count of inputs first observable inside the performance window is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]] and the count observable only after the outcome is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing evidence every input is available at the moment the score would be used and none of them can carry the outcome back into the score.\nThat is the right shape for a forward-looking default score, and it is the single most important design property to have established before any of the performance numbers are read.\n\nThe developer's own collinearity screen dropped two inputs before fitting.\nIt removed bill_last, whose variance inflation was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and utilisation_mean_6m, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against the screen's own cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].\nBoth removals are defensible on their face: a point-in-time bill level is close to redundant against the averaged bill level over the recent window, and an averaged utilisation is close to redundant against point-in-time utilisation, so retaining them would have destabilised the surviving coefficients without adding much that the retained pair does not already carry.\nThe consequence for interpretation is that the retained bill and utilisation coefficients absorb the influence of their dropped partners, and should be read as the effect of a bill-level block and a utilisation block rather than of narrowly ## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
